clue.text: Generous amount, say, on offer

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: to hand something to someone is to offer it

indicators.note: say signals that the word is spoken, so the spelling may change to a word of the same sound

parts.note: a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A big sum of money is being offered to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals a sound-alike: the money word is swapped for a common word that sounds the same. In an across clue 'on' means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome gift or payment is a large, liberal one, so the word is a synonym of generous.

clue.text: Slave labour building hotels

indicators.note: building means putting the letters of hotels together in a new structure

explanation.surface: Underpaid workers are being exploited to put up new hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' tells you to rearrange the letters of HOTELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the serf class of ancient Sparta, so the plural word stands for a body of slave workers.

clue.text: Study turned over, being infested? There, there

indicators.note: being here links the study to its state: the infestation sits inside it
turned over says the word for a study is read from the end back

parts.note: a den is a private room for work or study
what something infested is full of is vermin, pests such as rats or lice

explanation.surface: Someone's study, overturned, turns out to be crawling with pests, and they are told not to worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses the study word. 'being infested' implies pests living inside it, so the pest word goes in the middle. The definition is the soothing phrase said to an upset child.
explanation.definitionFit: Never mind and there, there are both soothing phrases said to comfort someone who is upset.

clue.text: Stonefish

definitions.meaning: a ... (sardius) is an old name for a red precious stone, as in the Bible's jasper and ... stone
a small oily fish of the herring family

explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like one word, stonefish, but splits into two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a biblical gemstone like sard and a small food fish, so each half defines it.

clue.text: Low at first, daughter's happy in the end .. being this?

definitions.text: Low at first, daughter's happy in the end .. being this?

parts.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes, moo
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: in the end picks only the final letter of happy

explanation.surface: Someone is down at first and then cheerful later on: what kind of person would that be?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: someone low, then happy, is changeable in temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A person whose spirits swing from low to happy is temperamental, which is what moody describes.

clue.text: Plant in mass behind wood

indicators.note: behind places the mass abbreviation after the wood

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood used for models
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A plant is growing in a clump behind some trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places M after BALSA. 'in' is only a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is a flowering garden plant, the impatiens, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Cynthia's painting newly-built semi

parts.note: painting is a form of art

indicators.note: newly-built says the letters of semi are put up in a new order

explanation.surface: Cynthia's picture shows a semi-detached house that has just been built.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly-built' rearranges the house. A semi is the British word for a semi-detached house. The 's after Cynthia stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: Cynthia is a classical title of the moon goddess, born on Mount Cynthus, who is the Greek huntress goddess.

clue.text: The author's a mug

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the setter calling themselves a fool, but it gives two definitions: a writer and a drinking vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Gertrude Stein was a modernist writer, and a stein is a German-style beer tankard.

clue.text: One driving round hill shrouded in fog

indicators.note: shrouded in means wrapped inside, so the fog surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: mist is a thin fog
O is round in shape
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A driver goes round a hill hidden in fog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shrouded in' wraps the fog around the circle and the hill. A tor is a rocky hilltop, typical of Dartmoor in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is a person who drives a car, so one driving defines them.

clue.text: Entire fleet's in a state of confusion

definitions.meaning: with every ship away on the water the whole fleet is out on the ocean
bewildered, not knowing what to do

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: if the entire fleet is out sailing, it is literally away on the sea. The 's means is.
explanation.definitionFit: All at sea is an idiom for being bewildered, and also says literally that every ship is sailing.

clue.text: Prime Minister's plane, perhaps, finally left London terminal

parts.note: Lord Liverpool was British Prime Minister from 1812 to 1827
the plane is an example of a tree

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of left

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister's aircraft finally took off from a London station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane' wants to be an aircraft; it is the tree. 'finally' takes the last letter of left. LIVERPOOL STREET is a main railway station in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool Street is a major railway terminus in the City of London.

clue.text: Scare old actress if making entrance towards the rear

indicators.note: making entrance towards the rear means going into the actress's name near its end

parts.note: Ellen Terry was a great Victorian stage actress

explanation.surface: An old actress gives the audience a fright by coming on from the back of the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making entrance towards the rear' sends the little word into the actress's surname near its end. Ellen Terry was a famous Victorian stage actress.
explanation.definitionFit: To terrify someone is to frighten them badly, so it is a stronger synonym of scare.

clue.text: Charity worker, an independent sort, collecting millions

indicators.note: collecting means taking another piece inside

parts.note: a loner is a person who keeps to themselves
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A charity worker who likes to work alone raises millions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collecting' puts M inside A LONER.
explanation.definitionFit: An almoner was an official who gave out alms, and later a hospital social worker, so a charity worker.

clue.text: Bistros devised new restrictions, closing about one

indicators.note: closing about means shutting around something, so the reordered letters hold one inside
devised means worked out afresh, so the letters of new are reordered

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
bars are restrictions or barriers

explanation.surface: Restaurants have come up with new rules on serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' scrambles new, and 'closing about' wraps that scramble round one (I) to make the drink, before the restrictions follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is a small, informal place to eat and drink, like a bistro.

clue.text: Corrupt senator's one who backs prospective candidate

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or bent out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of senator plus the s are all used

explanation.surface: A dishonest politician supports someone standing for office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges all the letters of SENATOR'S, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: An assentor is a voter who signs a nomination paper backing a candidate, in addition to the proposer and seconder.

clue.text: A doctor on board ship somewhere in the Aegean

indicators.note: on board means inside the ship, so the other pieces go within it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
MO is a medical officer

explanation.surface: A doctor is sailing on a cruise ship around the Greek islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' is the usual signal for going inside the ship's abbreviation, SS for steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean Sea, so it is a place in the Aegean.

clue.text: Dame Norma's broken records

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: the possessive s gives no letter

explanation.surface: Dame Norma has smashed several world records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges DAME NORMA. 'records' wants to be sporting records; they are written notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Memoranda, plural of memorandum, are written notes kept as records.

clue.text: Surrender accumulated prize money

definitions.meaning: to give up and submit, like a dog lying on its back
a lottery jackpot carried forward to the next draw when no one wins

explanation.definitionFit: To roll over is to give in without a fight, and a rollover is an unwon jackpot carried forward.

clue.text: Class given instruction

definitions.meaning: a rank or category, as in biology

explanation.definitionFit: An order is a rank in classification and also a command someone is given.

clue.text: Fried food is stodgy at first, in part

indicators.note: in places the other pieces within the word for a part

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of stodgy

explanation.surface: A fried dish is heavy, to begin with at least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes only the opening letter of stodgy; 'in' then places is plus that letter inside the part in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A rissole is a fried cake of minced meat or fish coated in breadcrumbs.

clue.text: I don't know how you'll find what's concealed on my person

definitions.meaning: a shrugging reply to a question you cannot answer

definitions.text: how you'll find what's concealed on my person
definitions.meaning: an invitation to frisk the speaker for anything hidden

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: to find something hidden on me, frisk me.
explanation.definitionFit: Search me is an idiom meaning I have no idea, and literally invites a frisk.

clue.text: Head off duck that's making for group

indicators.note: head off says the first letter of the duck's name goes

parts.note: a scoter is a dark sea duck
i.e. is the abbreviation of Latin id est, that is

explanation.surface: A duck sets off, leading the way towards the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' removes the first letter from SCOTER. 'making for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people with shared interests.

clue.text: Abridged version of second book on wine area

parts.note: Ex is the short form of Exodus, the second book of the Bible
tent is a deep red Spanish wine used for communion

explanation.surface: A shortened second volume deals with a wine-growing region.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. Tent is an old name for a sweet Spanish red wine, met mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means the size or area something covers.

clue.text: First play spades, regularly taking tricks

parts.note: the lead is the first card played in a trick
S is the abbreviation for spades in bridge
someone who is on a drug takes it regularly

explanation.surface: A card player opens with a spade and keeps winning tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricks' looks like the card-game noun but is the definition, a verb meaning deceives.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to deceive or mislead them, so it means tricks.

clue.text: Collection of trees gardener's planted

indicators.note: planted means set into the soil, so the answer is buried inside the word

explanation.surface: A group of trees has been put in by a gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted' says the answer is set inside gardener's. The Forest of Arden is an English forest, the setting of As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: Arden is the name of an old forest in Warwickshire, so a collection of trees.

clue.text: Gallic hero, mostly grim-faced, enters town in Provence

indicators.note: enters means goes into the town

parts.note: Aix-en-Provence is a town in southern France

indicators.note: mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: stern means grim or severe

explanation.surface: A French hero, looking grim, marches into a southern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the grim-faced word; 'enters' puts what remains into the Provence town, Aix-en-Provence.
explanation.definitionFit: Asterix is the Gaulish warrior hero of the French comic books, so a hero from Gaul.

clue.text: Boy regularly ejected by tall officer

indicators.note: regularly ejected by means every other letter of tall officer is thrown out, leaving the rest

explanation.surface: A lad is thrown out regularly by a tall policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ejected by' drops T, L, O, F, C, R and keeps the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfie is a boy's name, a pet form of Alfred.

clue.text: Discussion bringing together widely-separated views

parts.note: reads like a debate that reconciles opposing opinions, but the views are screen images of people far apart

explanation.surface: A debate reconciles very different opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'views' wants to be opinions; it is the pictures on screens linking distant people.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting held over video links connects people in far-apart places, each seen on screen.

clue.text: Shoot the messenger

definitions.meaning: a new stem growing from a plant, such as a strawberry

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the saying don't shoot the messenger, but gives two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is a creeping plant stem and also someone who carries messages.

clue.text: Left expert to make comeback in pilot TV show

indicators.note: in means inside the word for a pilot

parts.note: a pilot scheme is a test

indicators.note: to make comeback means the word for expert is read backwards

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: An expert who left returns in a trial episode of a TV programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make comeback' reverses the expert; 'in' puts left and that reversal inside the pilot, a pilot being a trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A telecast is a programme broadcast on television.
